items.informal_name: Linear Independence of Variables in Multivariate Polynomial Ring
items.type: ∀ (σ : Type u) (R : Type v) [inst : CommSemiring R], LinearIndependent R MvPolynomial.X
items.informal_description: The family of variables in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ is linearly independent over $ R $, meaning that no non-trivial finite $ R $-linear combination of these variables equals zero.

items.informal_name: Linear Independence of Polynomial Sequence Basis
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Ring R] (S : Polynomial.Sequence R) [IsDomain R], LinearIndependent R ↑S
items.informal_description: The family of monomials in the sequence representation of polynomials forms a linearly independent set in the module structure over the semiring $ R $. Specifically, no non-trivial linear combination of these monomials with coefficients in $ R $ yields the zero polynomial.

items.informal_name: Linear Independence of Evaluated Partial Derivatives of Relations in Submersive Presentation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {ι : Type w} {σ : Type t} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  [inst_3 : Finite σ] (P : Algebra.SubmersivePresentation R S ι σ),
  LinearIndependent S fun i j => (MvPolynomial.aeval P.val) ((MvPolynomial.pderiv (P.map j)) (P.relation i))
items.informal_description: The family of elements in $ S $ obtained by evaluating the partial derivatives of the relations in a submersive presentation $ P $ at the generators of $ S $ is linearly independent over $ S $. Specifically, for all indices $ i, j $, the evaluation map $ \text{aeval} $ applied to the partial derivative $ \text{pderiv}_{P.\text{map}(j)}(P.\text{relation}(i)) $ yields a linearly independent set in $ S $.

items.informal_name: Algebraic Independence of Polynomials from Evaluation Independence
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u} {R : Type u_2} {A : Type v} {x : ι → A} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A]
  {f : ι → MvPolynomial ι R}, (AlgebraicIndependent R fun i => (MvPolynomial.aeval x) (f i)) → AlgebraicIndependent R f
items.informal_description: If the evaluations of a family of multivariate polynomials $ f_i $ at a point $ x $ form an algebraically independent set over $ R $, then the original polynomials $ f_i $ are algebraically independent over $ R $. This means that whenever $ \{\text{aeval}_x(f_i)\} $ has no non-trivial polynomial relations over $ R $, the polynomials $ \{f_i\} $ themselves also have no non-trivial polynomial relations over $ R $.

items.informal_name: Trivial Kernel of Evaluation Map on Bounded Exponent Multivariate Polynomials
items.type: ∀ (σ K : Type u) [inst : Fintype K] [inst_1 : Field K] [Finite σ], (MvPolynomial.evalᵢ σ K).ker = ⊥
items.informal_description: For a finite commutative ring $ K $ and type $ \sigma $, the kernel of the $ K $-linear evaluation map on the submodule of multivariate polynomials $ K[\sigma] $ with exponents in each variable at most $ \#K - 1 $ is trivial, containing only the zero polynomial. This means the evaluation map is injective when restricted to this submodule.

items.informal_name: Evaluation Preserves Algebraic Independence
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u} {R : Type u_2} {A : Type v} {x : ι → A} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A],
  AlgebraicIndependent R x →
    ∀ {f : ι → MvPolynomial ι R},
      AlgebraicIndependent R f → AlgebraicIndependent R fun i => (MvPolynomial.aeval x) (f i)
items.informal_description: If a family of multivariate polynomials $ f_i $ is algebraically independent over a commutative semiring $ R $, then evaluating each polynomial at a fixed element $ x $ via the algebra homomorphism $ \text{aeval} $ preserves their algebraic independence over $ R $. In other words, the evaluated family $ (\text{aeval}_x(f_i)) $ remains algebraically independent in the target algebra.

items.informal_name: Algebraic Independence Implies Linear Independence
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u} {R : Type u_2} {A : Type v} {x : ι → A} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A],
  AlgebraicIndependent R x → LinearIndependent R x
items.informal_description: If a set $ x $ of elements in an $ R $-algebra $ A $ is algebraically independent over $ R $, then it is linearly independent over $ R $.

items.informal_name: Characterization of Algebraic Independence via Supported Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_2} {A : Type v} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] {s : Set A},
  AlgebraicIndependent R Subtype.val ↔ ∀ p ∈ MvPolynomial.supported R s, (MvPolynomial.aeval id) p = 0 → p = 0
items.informal_description: A set $ s $ in an $ R $-algebra $ A $ is algebraically independent over $ R $ if and only if every polynomial in the variables of $ s $ (i.e., supported on $ s $) that evaluates to zero in $ A $ must be the zero polynomial. This establishes the equivalence between algebraic independence and the injectivity of the evaluation homomorphism restricted to polynomials supported on $ s $.

items.informal_description: A set $ s $ in an $ R $-algebra $ A $ is algebraically independent over $ R $ if and only if every polynomial in the variables of $ s $ (i.e., supported on $ s $) that evaluates to zero in $ A $ must be the zero polynomial. This establishes the equivalence between algebraic independence and the injectivity of the evaluation homomorphism restricted to polynomials supported on $ s $.
